s1.syndrome_frame: Acute decompensated heart failure with arrhythmia
salient_findings: New York Heart Association functional class IV symptoms
key_facts: Patient has a history of ischemic cardiomyopathy
Ejection fraction is 10%
Patient has a single-chamber primary prevention implantable cardioverter-defibrillator
Patient was previously on amiodarone treatment
Heart rate is 106 beats/min
Blood pressure is 96/58 mm Hg
N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide is markedly elevated
Creatinine levels are elevated
ECG shows a wide QRS rhythm with atypical left bundle-branch block morphology
Electrophysiology study confirmed dual tachycardia

shortlist.label: Ischemic cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of ischemic cardiomyopathy and decreased ejection fraction

shortlist.label: Tachycardia-induced cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has dual tachycardia confirmed by electrophysiology study and decreased ejection fraction

shortlist.label: Cardiogenic shock
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has signs of substantial volume overload, elevated jugular venous pressure, and decreased ejection fraction

shortlist.label: Acute coronary syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of ischemic cardiomyopathy and elevated creatinine levels

shortlist.label: Ventricular tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a wide QRS rhythm with atypical left bundle-branch block morphology and dual tachycardia confirmed by electrophysiology study

raw.rationale: The patient presents with signs of substantial volume overload, elevated jugular venous pressure, bilateral lung crackles, and a prominent S3 on cardiac auscultation, indicating severe heart failure. The markedly elevated N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide and decreased ejection fraction of 10% further support this diagnosis. The patient's hypotension (blood pressure 96/58 mm Hg) and tachycardia (heart rate 106 beats/min) are also consistent with cardiogenic shock.

rejected.label: Ischemic cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of ischemic cardiomyopathy, this diagnosis does not fully explain the acute presentation of worsening shortness of breath and hypotension.

rejected.label: Tachycardia-induced cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The patient's ejection fraction was already severely decreased (10%) at baseline, making it less likely that tachycardia is the primary cause of cardiomyopathy.

rejected.label: Acute coronary syndrome
rejected.why: There is no clear evidence of acute coronary syndrome, such as chest pain or ECG changes indicative of ischemia.

rejected.label: Ventricular tachycardia
rejected.why: While the electrophysiology study confirmed dual tachycardia, the patient's presentation is more consistent with cardiogenic shock due to severe heart failure rather than a primary arrhythmic diagnosis.
